answer: At dawn, fixed-pool dilution opens a 40,000-credit pool that never grows. Each identity pays 45 and locks an opal bond of 70 for a share. The beacon binds each bond to one key; false claims burn the bond. 1,000 fakes burn 45,000 chasing a pool capped at 40,000, a sure 5,000 loss; each fake dilutes the attacker's own share. Rented-bond rings fail: the beacon burns a bond backing two claims. One honest agent pays 45 once and keeps a full share.
